governingStatute: Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 read with Section 133 of Companies Act, 2013 and US GAAP FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 606
statutorySection: Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) converged with IFRS 15 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 606
title: Revenue from Contracts with Customers (5-Step Transaction Price Allocation & Performance Obligation Recognition)

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Continuous contract modification, allocation, and milestone true-ups at reporting dates
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Mandatory standard notified via MCA G.S.R. 310(E) effective FY 2018-19 onwards.

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 115 (converged with IFRS 15 and substantially aligned with US GAAP ASC 606), revenue is recognized upon the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled. The standard enforces a uniform, mandatory five-step revenue framework: (1) Identify the contract with a customer; (2) Identify the performance obligations in the contract, distinguishing between distinct goods or services; (3) Determine the transaction price, taking into account variable consideration (discounts, rebates, refunds, penalties) subject to the constraint that a significant reversal must be highly probable not to occur; (4) Allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation on a relative Standalone Selling Price (SSP) basis; and (5) Recognize revenue when or as the entity satisfies a performance obligation, either over time (if the customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits, the entity creates/enhances a customer-controlled asset, or the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date with no alternative use) or at a point in time. When consideration is received or due prior to performance, the entity recognizes a Contract Liability (Deferred Revenue). When performance is completed prior to unconditional billing entitlement, the entity recognizes a Contract Asset (Unbilled Revenue). For dual-reporting entities (e.g. US Delaware Parent and Indian Subsidiary), revenue recognition schedules must reconcile cross-border contract allocations against both US GAAP ASC 606 and Indian Income Computation and Disclosure Standard IV (ICDS IV).

requiredDocumentChecklist: Master Services Agreement (MSA) and all executed Statements of Work (SOWs) / Change Orders
Standalone Selling Price (SSP) documentation and observable price methodology
Customer acceptance certificates or milestone achievement sign-offs
Contract Asset (unbilled revenue) and Contract Liability (deferred revenue) roll-forward schedule
Variable consideration estimation workpaper showing constraint evaluation
Dual-standard reconciliation reconciling Ind AS 115 revenue with US GAAP ASC 606 and ICDS IV
